docs.alert.a11y.action: An action in the body is a native button or link, reached with Tab in the order of the page, with the focus ring of its own component.
docs.alert.a11y.contrast: The title and the body have at least 4.5:1 against the background of every tone, in the light and the dark theme. A color of your own through className is yours to check.
docs.alert.a11y.live: With live it is role="alert" in the red tone and role="status" in the others. Use it only for a message that appears after an action: one that is there on load would interrupt the reader before the user has done anything.
docs.alert.a11y.mounted: A screen reader announces what changes inside a live region that already exists. Keep the Alert mounted and change its title and children when the message arrives; one that is added together with its message may go unannounced, status ones above all.
docs.alert.a11y.static: Without live it has no role: a div that a screen reader reads in the flow of the page, as any other content.
docs.alert.a11y.strings: Alert has no text of its own: the title, the body and the label of an action are yours, in the language of your page, and a FormaProvider changes nothing here.
docs.alert.a11y.text: Color is never the only thing that says what an alert means. The title says it, and the tone reinforces it.
docs.alert.action.description: The body is children, so an action is a Button or a link inside it. There is no action prop.
docs.alert.action.hint: Not live here: it is part of the page from the start. Add live when the error appears after an action.
docs.alert.action.title: With an action
docs.alert.api.children: The body of the alert. It can hold a Button or a link for an action. Without children, no body is drawn.
docs.alert.api.className: Added after the library's own class names.
docs.alert.api.live: Makes the alert a live region: role="alert" for red, role="status" for the other tones. For a message that appears after an action; keep the alert mounted while its text changes.
docs.alert.api.others: Every other attribute of the native div element goes to it as it is: id, aria-*, data-*, the event handlers and ref.
docs.alert.api.role: Without live there is none. A role that you pass wins over the one that live sets.
docs.alert.api.title: The heading of the alert, always visible. It replaces the native title tooltip attribute and is required.
docs.alert.api.tone: The color role of the alert. It colors the alert and says nothing by itself: its title must say the same thing.
docs.alert.limit.action: There is no action prop: the action is a child, laid out after the text in the body.
docs.alert.limit.design: The component comes from Resolve with its API unchanged. The title has margin: 0 of its own, so it does not depend on your reset; in Resolve, whose reset already zeroes it, nothing changes. An empty body (null, false, an empty string or array) is not drawn.
docs.alert.limit.dismiss: There is no close button, so the library has no text for one: if the user may dismiss an alert, put a button with your own label in the body and remove the alert in your state.
docs.alert.limit.icon: It has no icon: the title and the color carry the meaning. Put an Icon in the title if you need one.
docs.alert.limit.tones: There are four tones and no neutral one: a message that none of them fits is not an alert.
docs.alert.live.description: With live an alert is announced to a screen reader. Use it for a message that appears after an action, never for one that is there when the page loads.
docs.alert.live.hint: Press Save: the same alert changes its text, which is what gets announced.
docs.alert.live.redHint: An error is role="alert", which interrupts. The alert is empty when the page loads and the message arrives when you press the button, as an error does in an application.
docs.alert.live.title: Live region
docs.alert.readOnly.description: An amber alert that is there when the page loads tells the user that the document cannot be edited, and may offer a way out.
docs.alert.readOnly.hint: Not live: it is part of the page from the start, so it is read in order and does not interrupt.
docs.alert.readOnly.title: Read-only strip
docs.alert.summary: A message that stays on the page, with a title and a body, in four tones.
docs.alert.tones.description: Four color roles: blue for information, green for success, amber for a warning and red for an error. Each one has the same layout.
docs.alert.tones.title: Tones
docs.alert.usage.description: Import Alert, give it a title and write the body as its children. The tone only colors it: the title is what says what it means.
